Subject: Next steps: Technical deep-dive with ML/Infra team (60-90m) - Acme Health Tech

Hi Ava -

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery: Acme is looking to standardize inference for multi-model clinical summarization pipelines, prioritize latency under 200ms 99th percentile for short prompts, and keep inference costs predictable across production. You mentioned Rahul (ML infra) and a couple of infra folks should join the deep-dive to validate performance and integration patterns.

Proposed next step: a 60-90 minute technical deep-dive with your ML + infra team where we can cover:
- high-level architecture & data flow
- model variants and quantization options
- latency & throughput targets, batching strategy
- caching (prefix/KV) and stateful sessions
- security, data residency, and KMS/HSM integration
- benchmarking plan & success criteria

I attached a short proposed agenda and a blank data-flow diagram for your team to annotate. Could you confirm who from Rahul's team should attend and share 2-3 time slots? I'm available next week (Tue/Wed/Thu mornings PT).

Agenda draft attached: redwood-technical-deep-dive-agenda.pdf
Diagram attached: acme-data-flow-diagram.png

Thanks - looking forward to aligning calendars.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
https://redwood.com

Thanks Ava - Tue 24 Mar 10:00-11:30 PT works well for us. Marking as a 90-minute slot so we have flexibility.

Updated agenda (attached and pasted below) - please let me know if you'd like to reorder or add topics. Pre-reads: 1) short note on our benchmarking methodology (link below), 2) annotated data-flow (attached) - if Rahul's team can add notes to the diagram ahead of time that will speed the session.

90-min technical deep-dive agenda (Marissa / Dev / David will lead sections)
- 0-10m: Introductions & goals (confirm success criteria)
- 10-30m: Acme current architecture & integration points (Rahul + infra)
- 30-50m: Serving runtime & model variant options (Marissa) - quantization, kernels, memory/latency tradeoffs
- 50-70m: Batching, caching, and KV state management (Dev) - expected impact on p50/p99 and perf/cost tradeoffs
- 70-85m: Security & deployment options (David) - VPC/private, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- 85-90m: Next steps & action items

Pre-reads/links:
- Benchmarking methodology: https://redwood.app/s/ACME-12345-call-notes
- Calendar invite (placeholder): https://cal.com/marissa/redwood-technical-deep-dive

Attachments: redwood-technical-deep-dive-agenda.pdf, acme-data-flow-diagram.png

If that looks good I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in and include a shared Google Doc for running notes.
